name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,186

clue.text: Places where people call xenophobes out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, as in a calculation that is out, so the letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters for the whole answer

explanation.surface: Someone urges the public to denounce those who hate foreigners wherever they find them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call xenophobes out' reads as a single phrase meaning to condemn bigots, but 'call' belongs to the definition and 'out' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Public telephone kiosks are booths where passers-by make telephone calls.

clue.text: Honoured bard out late, cavorting with a peer

indicators.note: cavorting is leaping about wildly, so the letters jump into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrated poet is out on the town late at night, carousing with a member of the nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is split across 'with': 'out late' and 'a peer' together supply all twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of this official post is a poet given royal or national recognition, hence an honoured writer of verse.

clue.text: Start working as a film director, perhaps

definitions.text: working as a film director, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: a beginning

blocks.clueFragment: working as a film director, perhaps
blocks.note: second meaning, split as two words: present at the place where a film is shot

explanation.surface: Advice to begin a career by taking up film directing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into ON SET, where a director works; 'perhaps' marks a director as just one example of who is found there.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something, such as an illness or winter, is called its commencement or first arrival.

clue.text: Devious type ultimately made everyone distrustful

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of each following word counts

blocks.note: the final letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A sly character eventually left the whole group suspicious of one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' looks like a time adverb for the sentence, but it picks the last letter of each of the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slippery and evasive is called an eel, after the wriggling fish that is hard to grasp.

clue.text: Periodically dour, thoroughly dystopian author

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
well can mean thoroughly, as in mix well

explanation.surface: A description of a gloomy novelist: grim now and then, and wholly bleak in outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: George Orwell wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four, the classic dystopian novel.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell is famous for the bleak future society imagined in Nineteen Eighty-Four, so he is a writer of dystopias.

clue.text: All at the finish are incredibly on edge

definitions.note: the answer is an adverbial phrase meaning completely

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its end, so its closing letter is taken

blocks.note: the final letter
both are intensifiers meaning extremely
to edge forward is to inch along

explanation.surface: At the end of a race, every competitor is incredibly nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' looks like a phrase meaning nervous, but 'on' only places one piece after another in this down clue, and 'edge' is a verb for creeping forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Every inch means entirely or in all respects, as in every inch a gentleman, matching all used adverbially.

clue.text: Farewell single, no good

blocks.note: a solo is a performance by one person alone
NG is the standard abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Someone says goodbye to the bachelor life, calling it worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' suggests an unmarried person or a record, but here it means one alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal ways of saying goodbye when parting company with someone.

clue.text: New athletes turn up and have surprising success

indicators.note: something new is a fresh version, so the letters are made over into a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
to turn up is to show up or appear

explanation.surface: Fresh competitors arrive at an event and unexpectedly win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like it belongs with the athletes arriving, but it is the synonym for the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine everyone else unexpectedly, drawing all the attention and praise, is an idiom from the theatre.

clue.text: Supporter of the arts?

blocks.note: surface reading: a patron who funds painters and musicians
setter's reading: a wooden stand that literally holds up a painter's canvas

explanation.walkthrough: A supporter usually means a backer or patron; here it is a physical prop, and the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's frame physically holds the canvas upright while artwork is made, so it literally bears up art.

clue.text: Eliminate small feeling of uncertainty, by the sounds of it

indicators.note: judging by the sound means the words are heard rather than read, so a spoken match is wanted

blocks.note: wee is Scottish and British for small, and a doubt is a feeling of uncertainty; the B in doubt is silent

explanation.surface: Advice to get rid of even a slight hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, WEE DOUBT matches WEED OUT; the silent B in doubt does not sound. 'Wee' is the Scottish word for small.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove unwanted members from a group is like pulling unwanted plants from a garden.

clue.text: Really recover following diet

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: lite is the marketing spelling for low-calorie diet food
to rally is to recover strength

explanation.surface: An exclamation about making a genuine comeback after dieting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' is not a noun for eating less but an adjective sense, as in diet cola, which is LITE.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday speech the word is an intensifier meaning truly or actually, the same use as really.

clue.text: Assign position again to gather what is relevant

blocks.note: to reap is to gather a harvest
the point is the relevant matter, as in to the point

explanation.surface: Reassigning someone's role so they can collect pertinent information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What is relevant' is the point of a discussion, as in sticking to the point.
explanation.definitionFit: To name a person once more to a job or office they held before is the meaning here.

clue.text: Eggs, mostly egg-shaped!

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: oval describes an egg-like outline

explanation.surface: An exclamation that eggs are, for the most part, egg-shaped.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a deliberately obvious statement; the answer is OVAL with its last letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin-derived plural of ovum, the biological term for egg cells.

clue.text: Extreme component of long-haul travel

indicators.note: a component is a part of a whole, so the letters are a run inside the phrase

blocks.note: the end of haul runs into the start of travel

explanation.surface: Something extreme is a feature of travelling very long distances.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts inside 'haul' and ends inside 'travel', across the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or adjective it means beyond the usual, radical or excessive, as in ultra-conservative.

clue.text: Swimmers crowding river channel

indicators.note: to crowd something is to press around it, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: tench are freshwater fish; the plural is the same as the singular
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Swimmers bunch together in a narrow river channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmers' means fish here: a tench is a European freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow ditch dug in the ground, or a deep furrow on the sea floor, is a kind of channel.

clue.text: Nearly time for hours of darkness

blocks.note: nigh means nearly, as in nigh on
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It is almost the moment for the dark hours to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' reads as a deletion signal but is a plain synonym for NIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The period between sunset and sunrise is when it is dark outside.

clue.text: Coin in small opening

blocks.note: taken as written
a vent is a small hole letting air or gas escape

explanation.surface: A coin has been pushed into a small slot, as in a vending machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coin' is a verb, as in to coin a phrase; and 'in' is not a container signal but letters taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a word or phrase is to make up something new, the same as devising or creating it.

clue.text: Closely examine part of potato

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to look at carefully
second meaning: the bud on a tuber from which shoots grow

explanation.surface: Instructions to inspect a section of a potato carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: A potato's small buds, from which new shoots sprout, share their name with the organ of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to watch or scrutinize; as a noun it names the sprouting bud on a tuber.

clue.text: Writer heading for town to take in luxury flat

indicators.note: the heading of something is its top, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the opening letter
to house someone is to take them in and give them shelter

explanation.surface: An author travels into the city to see an expensive apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' looks like a container signal but is a synonym, to give lodging. A flat is the British word for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: An expensive apartment on the top floor of a tall building is a classic example of a luxury home.

clue.text: Typical America university starts to accept loans

indicators.note: the start of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letters are kept

blocks.note: US is short for the United States of America
U is the abbreviation for university
the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A typical American college begins taking on student debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' reads as 'begins to' in the surface, but it picks the first letters of the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something normal or customary, the ordinary case, is what one expects as standard.

clue.text: Touching performance in hat, once

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: an act is a performance on stage
tile is old slang for a hat; once marks it as dated

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a moving show once given while wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' suggests moving or emotional, but here it means relating to touch. Tile was nineteenth-century slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things perceived through the sense of touch, or people who like physical contact.

clue.text: Pinkish, black and very green?

definitions.note: the clue gives an adjective; the answer is usually a noun naming that pale pink shade

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
lush vegetation is richly green and thick

explanation.surface: A list of colours that sounds like a confused description of something pink, black and green.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as three colours, but only the first is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Blush is a pale rosy tint, named after the reddening of cheeks, used for wines and fabrics.

clue.text: Bill raised for sporting equipment

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting something up turns it bottom to top

blocks.note: a tab is a bill or account, as at a bar

explanation.surface: A charge has gone up for buying sports gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name or a beak, but it is a tab to be paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A bat is the club used to strike the ball in cricket and baseball, a piece of gear for games.

clue.text: Volunteers express disappointment in Wales about legislation

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the opposite way, so the letters run backwards
to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the TA, or Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve army
tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
taken as written

explanation.surface: Volunteers in Wales voice their dismay over a piece of legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' but turns WALES backwards; the Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer military reserve, abbreviated TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Law enacted by a parliament as written acts, rather than arising from court decisions, is legislation.
